preamble: The voiced alveolar affricate [dz] (POJ j-) merges with the lateral [l] in Quanzhou-type Hokkien. Where Zhangzhou-type varieties keep the Proto-Southern Min voiced initial (from Middle Chinese 日 nasal initials) as [dz] or [z], Quanzhou, Xiamen and the Taipei and Lukang accents of Taiwan pronounce it [l], so the Taiwanese Hokkien dialect continuum shows both outcomes. The change is well documented but confined to Southern Min.

examples.note: Taipei and Lukang follow the Quanzhou-type [l] outcome; Kaohsiung has fricative /zi³³/.
Most Quanzhou dialects have no /dz/ initial, having merged it into /l/.
